name: Kiln & Co Ceramics
notes: Strong product photography. About page is two lines. No email capture on site. Reels exist but no one speaks to camera. Only 4 product descriptions mention how the pieces are made.

gaps.summary: The product looks good and says almost nothing about the people or process behind it. There is no route from a visit to a relationship.
gaps.hook: The photography is excellent, but only four product pages say how the pieces are made, and there is no email signup to keep a visitor.

items.finding: Making process is the differentiator for handmade ceramics and it appears on four product pages only.
items.evidence: Product page review in your notes.
items.fix: Add a short making-of block to every product and a studio film on the About page.

items.finding: No email capture, so every visitor who is not ready to buy is lost.
items.fix: Add a first-order offer and a post-purchase care guide sequence.

outreach.body:
Hi Meera, your photography is some of the best I have seen in homeware. One thing stood out: only four product pages say how the pieces are made, and there is no email signup to keep a visitor who is not ready to buy. Would a one-page teardown of both be useful?

Joel

fu1.body:
Meera, one idea on the process point. A 20 second clip of the wheel on each product page would do more than any copy. Happy to sketch where they would go.

Joel

log.text: First message sent via LinkedIn DM
